summary: Geshe Palden Drakpa worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He was librarian at Tibet House, New Delhi in 1985 and a visiting scholar at the University of Virginia in 1987.

Geshe Sonam Rinchen worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studying at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies from circa 1970 to 1980. He then served as a teacher at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives from circa 1978 to 2013.

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Geshe Tashi Tsering studied under Geshe Thubten Rinchen, at Sera Monastery (1971–1987), and at Gyuto Monastery (circa 1989–1990). He taught at Kopan Monastery, Gandhi Foundation College, and Jamyang Buddhist Centre.
Geshe Tsondru Namgyal is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies who earned Geshe degrees while studying at Drepung Monastery and Yungdrung Ling Monastery.

Geshe Wangyal studied under Agvan Dorjiev and at Drepung Monastery. A scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he held posts at the Tibetan Buddhist Learning Center (circa 1958–1983) and Columbia University (circa 1962–1972).

Specializing in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Geshe Yeshe Tobden studied at Sera Monastery (circa 1938–1963) and under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Geshe Lodoe Sangpo, and Chusang Rinpoche. He taught Buddhist philosophy at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies from circa 1969 to 1971.
Gessho Sasaki was a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at Otani University from circa 1898 to 1901 and subsequently held a post there from circa 1901 to 1926.

A scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Giacomella Orofino studied at the University of Naples "L'Orientale", under Raniero Gnoli, and at Sapienza University of Rome. Since circa 1993, she has taught at the University of Naples "L'Orientale".
Gianpaolo Vetturini is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed his PhD at the University of London under the supervision of Tadeusz Skorupski from circa 2002 to 2007.

Giei Honda was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Kyoto University (circa 1910–1913). He held academic posts at Rissho University from circa 1924 to 1953 and Kyoto University from 1934 to 1948.

Gikyo Ito worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics, studying at Kyoto University under Atsuuji Ashikaga (circa 1931–1934). He held posts at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (circa 1964–1973) and Kyoto Sangyo University (circa 1973–1980).

Gil Fronsdal works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Stanford University (circa 1993–1998) under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure, and held posts at the Insight Meditation Center (circa 1995) and Sati Center for Buddhist Studies (circa 1997).

Gilles Tarabout is an Indology and religious studies scholar who has served as a senior fellow at the CNRS since circa 1984, a member at EHESS, and exchange program director at the Fondation Maison des Sciences de l'Homme.
Gin Ling Liu is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under Hsing Yun and completed a PhD at the University of Hong Kong (circa 2003–2008) under the supervision of Jing Yin.

Giovanni Gentile was a philosopher who studied at Scuola Normale Superiore and the University of Florence. He held posts at Palermo, Pisa, Sapienza University of Rome, Scuola Normale Superiore, Bocconi University, and was president of IsMEO in 1933.

Giovanni Vacca was a scholar in Sinology and history/archaeology who studied at the University of Genoa (circa 1893–1897). He held posts at the University of Florence (circa 1911–1921) and Sapienza University of Rome (circa 1923–1947).

Giovanni Verardi specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Allahabad, Banaras Hindu University, and Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University, and held a post at Kyoto University.

Girindrasekhar Bose was an Indian scholar who studied at Presidency University, Medical College and Hospital, Kolkata, and the University of Calcutta. He held posts at Medical College and Hospital (1911–1915) and the University of Calcutta (1917–1949).

Gisho Nakano was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (circa 1914–1917). He held academic posts at Kyushu University (circa 1925–1954) and Koyasan University (circa 1958–1973).
Giuliana Martini is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who held posts at both the Italian School of East Asian Studies and Kyoto University in 2010.
